rows.note: Use 叻 as the all-purpose casual adjective for someone who is clever, socially capable, or generally book-smart.

example.english: You’re so smart, you finished your homework so quickly.
example.traditional: 你咁叻，份功課咁快就做完喇。
example.jyutping: nei5 gam3 lek1 fan6 gung1 fo3 gam3 faai3 zau6 zou6 jyun4 laa3

rows.note: Use 智能 before a technology noun when the device or vehicle has intelligent or automated behaviour.

example.english: This smart fridge knows how to place orders by itself.
example.traditional: 呢部智能雪櫃識得自己落單。
example.jyutping: ni1 bou6 zi3 nang4 syut3 gwai6 sik1 dak1 zi6 gei2 lok6 daan1

rows.note: Use 有型 for someone or something that looks stylish, fashionable, or impressively well put together.

example.english: They look really smart in that suit.
example.traditional: 佢着住套西裝，真係好有型。
example.jyutping: keoi5 zoek3 zyu6 tou3 sai1 zong1 zan1 hai6 hou2 jau5 jing4

rows.note: Use 串 when a person or remark is cheeky, cocky, or disrespectfully smart-alecky.

example.english: You’re being so smart; it’s really annoying.
example.traditional: 你講嘢咁串，真係好乞人憎。
example.jyutping: nei5 gong2 je5 gam3 cyun3 zan1 hai6 hou2 hat1 jan4 zang1
